plan: 2 Kings 23:1-20; 2 Chronicles 34:29-33; 2 Kings 23:21-28; 2 Chronicles 35:1-19; Nahum 1:1, 2-15; Nahum 2:1-13; Nahum 3:1-19

readings.title: The Book of the Covenant is Read
readings.subtitle: The sovereign and the people commit to follow YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [2 Kings 23:1] And the sovereign sent, and they gathered all the elders of Yehuḏah and Yerushalayim to him. [2] And the sovereign went up to the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with <dn>את</dn> all the men of Yehuḏah, and all the inhabitants of Yerushalayim with him, and the priests and the prophets and all the people, both small and great. And he read in their hearing <dn>את</dn> all the words of the Book of the Covenant which had been found in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [3] And the sovereign stood by the column and made a covenant before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to follow <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and to guard <dn>His</dn> commands and <dn>His</dn> witnesses and <dn>His</dn> laws, with all his heart and all his being, to establish <dn>את</dn> the words of this covenant that were written in this book. And all the people stood to the covenant.

readings.title: Purging the House of YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: Yoshiyahu removes the implements of idolatry from the Temple.
readings.text: [4] Then the sovereign commanded Ḥilqiyahu the high priest, and the priests of the second order, and the doorkeepers, to bring out of the Hěḵal of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>את</dn> all the objects that were made for Ba‛al, and for Ashěrah, and for all the host of the heavens. And he burned them outside Yerushalayim in the fields of Qiḏron, and took their ashes to Běyth Ěl. [5] And he put down <dn>את</dn> the black-robed priests whom the sovereigns of Yehuḏah had appointed to burn incense on the high places in the cities of Yehuḏah and in the places all around Yerushalayim, and those who burned incense to Ba‛al, to the sun, and to the moon, and to the constellations, and to all the host of the heavens. [6] And he brought out <dn>את</dn> the Ashěrah from the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to the wadi Qiḏron outside Yerushalayim, and burned it at the wadi Qiḏron and ground it to ashes, and threw <dn>את</dn> its ashes on the burial-sites of the sons of the people. [7] And he broke down <dn>את</dn> the houses of the male cult prostitutes that were in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, where the women wove tapestries for the Ashěrah.

readings.title: Cleansing the Land of Yehuḏah
readings.subtitle: The reforms extend from Geḇa to Be’ěrsheḇa, defiling the high places.
readings.text: [8] And he brought <dn>את</dn> all the priests from the cities of Yehuḏah, and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense, from Geḇa to Be’ěrsheḇa, and broke down the high places at the gates which were at the entrance of the Gate of Yehoshua the governor of the city, which were to the left of the city gate. [9] However, the priests of the high places did not come up to the slaughter-place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in Yerushalayim, but they ate unleavened bread among their brothers. [10] And he defiled <dn>את</dn> Topheth, which is in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, so that no man could make his son or his daughter pass through the fire to Moleḵ. [11] And he did away with <dn>את</dn> the horses that the sovereigns of Yehuḏah had given to the sun, at the entrance to the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, by the room of Nathan-Meleḵ the eunuch, that were in the court. And he burned <dn>את</dn> the chariots of the sun with fire. [12] And <dn>את</dn> the slaughter-places that were on the roof of the upper room of Aḥaz, which the sovereigns of Yehuḏah had made, and <dn>את</dn> the slaughter-places which Menashsheh had made in the two courtyards of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the sovereign broke down, and rushed from there, and threw their dust into the wadi Qiḏron. [13] And the sovereign defiled <dn>את</dn> the high places that were before Yerushalayim, which were on the right hand of the Mountain of Destruction, which Shelomoh sovereign of Yisra’ěl built for Ashtoreth the abomination of the Tsiḏonians, and for Kemosh the abomination of the Mo’aḇites, and for Milkom the abomination of the children of Ammon. [14] And he broke in pieces <dn>את</dn> the pillars and cut down <dn>את</dn> the Ashěrim, and filled their places with the bones of men.

readings.title: The Altar at Běyth Ěl Destroyed
readings.subtitle: Yoshiyahu fulfills the prophecy of the man of Elohim.
readings.text: [15] And also <dn>את</dn> the slaughter-place that was at Běyth Ěl, and the high place which Yaroḇ‛am son of Neḇat made, by which he made Yisra’ěl sin, both that slaughter-place and the high place he broke down. And he burned the high place and ground it to dust, and burned <dn>את</dn> the Ashěrah. [16] Then Yoshiyahu turned, and saw the burial-sites that were there on the mountain. And he sent and took <dn>את</dn> the bones out of the burial-sites and burned them on the slaughter-place, and defiled it according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> proclaimed, who proclaimed these words. [17] And he said, “What tombstone is this that <dn>I</dn> see?” And the men of the city said to him, “It is the burial-site of the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> who came from Yehuḏah and proclaimed these matters which you have done against the slaughter-place of Běyth Ěl.” [18] And he said, “Let him alone, let no one move his bones.” So they left his bones alone, with <dn>את</dn> the bones of the prophet who came from Shomeron. [19] And Yoshiyahu also took away <dn>את</dn> all the houses of the high places that were in the cities of Shomeron, which the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl had made to provoke. And he did to them according to all the deeds he did in Běyth Ěl. [20] And he slaughtered <dn>את</dn> all the priests of the high places who were there, on the slaughter-places, and burned men’s bones on them, and went back to Yerushalayim.

readings.title: A Passover Without Precedent
readings.subtitle: In the eighteenth year of his reign, Yoshiyahu holds a great Pěsaḥ.
readings.text: [21] And the sovereign commanded <dn>את</dn> all the people, saying, “Prepare the Pěsaḥ to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, as it is written in this Book of the Covenant.” [22] For such a Pěsaḥ had not been prepared since the days of the rulers who ruled Yisra’ěl, nor in all the days of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl and the sovereigns of Yehuḏah, [23] but in the eighteenth year of Sovereign Yoshiyahu this Pěsaḥ was prepared before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in Yerushalayim.

readings.title: A Righteous Sovereign
readings.subtitle: Despite Yoshiyahu's zeal, YeHoVaH's wrath against Yehuḏah remains.
readings.text: [24] And also, Yoshiyahu put away those who consulted mediums and spiritists, and the household mighty ones and idols, and all the abominations that were seen in the land of Yehuḏah and in Yerushalayim, in order to establish <dn>את</dn> the words of the Torah which were written in the book that Ḥilqiyahu the priest found in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [25] And before him there was no sovereign like him, who turned back to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with all his heart, and with all his being, and with all his might, according to all the Torah of Mosheh; and after him none rose up like him. [26] However, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> did not turn from the fierceness of <dn>His</dn> great wrath, with which <dn>His</dn> wrath burned against Yehuḏah, because of all the provocations with which Menashsheh had provoked <dn>Him</dn>. [27] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“Even Yehuḏah <dn>I</dn> shall remove from <dn>My</dn> presence, as <dn>I</dn> have removed Yisra’ěl, and <dn>I</dn> shall reject this city Yerushalayim which <dn>I</dn> have chosen, and the House of which <dn>I</dn> said, ‘<dn>My</dn> Name is there.’ ”</dq> [28] And the rest of the acts of Yoshiyahu, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah?

readings.title: The Wrath and Power of YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: He is a jealous and revenging El, yet a stronghold for those who trust in Him.
readings.text: [Nahum 1:1] The message concerning Ninevěh. The book of the vision of Naḥum the Elqoshite. [2] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is a jealous and revenging <dn>Ěl</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is a revenger and a possessor of wrath. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> takes vengeance on <dn>His</dn> adversaries, and <dn>He</dn> watches for <dn>His</dn> enemies. [3] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is patient and great in power, but by no means leaves unpunished. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has <dn>His</dn> way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of <dn>His</dn> feet. [4] <dn>He</dn> is rebuking the sea and dries it up. And all the floods <dn>He</dn> has made dry, Bashan and Karmel are withering, and the flower of Leḇanon is languishing. [5] Mountains have shaken before <dn>Him</dn>, and the hills have melted. And the earth is lifted up at <dn>His</dn> presence, and the world and all who dwell in it. [6] Who does stand before <dn>His</dn> rage? And who rises up in the heat of <dn>His</dn> displeasure? <dn>His</dn> wrath is poured out like fire, and the rocks have been broken by <dn>Him</dn>. [7] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is good, as a stronghold in the day of distress. And <dn>He</dn> knows those who take refuge in <dn>Him</dn>. [8] But with an overwhelming flood <dn>He</dn> makes a complete end of the place of Ninevěh, and darkness does pursue <dn>His</dn> enemies.

readings.title: Nineveh's End, Yehuḏah's Peace
readings.subtitle: The wicked counsellor will be cut off, and the yoke will be broken from Yehuḏah.
readings.text: [9] What do you plot against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>? <dn>He</dn> makes a complete end of it. Distress does not rise up a second time. [10] Though they are as entangled thorns, and as drunkards with their drink, they shall be consumed like stubble thoroughly dried. [11] From you came forth one who plots evil against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, a counsellor of Beliya‛al. [12] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Though they are strong and many, even so, they shall be cut off and pass away. Though <dn>I</dn> have afflicted you, <dn>I</dn> afflict you no more.</dq> [13] <dq>“So now <dn>I</dn> break his yoke from you, and tear off your shackles.”</dq> [14] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has commanded concerning you, <dq>“Your name shall no longer be sown. From the house of your mighty ones <dn>I</dn> shall cut off the carved image and the moulded image. <dn>I</dn> shall appoint your burial-site, for you have been of no account.”</dq> [15] See, on the mountains the feet of him who brings good news, who proclaims peace! O Yehuḏah, celebrate your festivals, perform your vows. For Beliya‛al shall no more pass through you. <dn>He</dn> has been cut off completely.

readings.title: The Destroyer Comes
readings.subtitle: A vivid depiction of the assault on the city's ramparts.
readings.text: [Nahum 2:1] He who breaks in pieces has come up before your face. Guard the ramparts! Watch the way! Strengthen your loins! Fortify your power very much. [2] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall turn back the splendour of Ya‛aqoḇ like the splendour of Yisra’ěl, for the emptiers have emptied them out and ruined their vine branches. [3] The shields of his mighty men have become red, the men of battle are in scarlet. The chariots are like flaming torches in the day of his preparation, and the cypresses shall be shaken. [4] The chariots dash about in the streets, they rush one another in the broad ways. They look like flaming torches, they run like lightning. [5] He remembers his noble ones, they stumble in their walk, they hurry to her walls, and the defence is prepared. [6] The river gates have been opened, and the palace is melted. [7] And it is established: she shall be exiled, she shall be led away. And her female servants are moaning as with the voice of doves, beating on their breasts.

readings.title: The Lion's Den is Emptied
readings.subtitle: Nineveh is plundered of its wealth, and its heart melts in terror.
readings.text: [8] And Ninevěh of old was like a pool of water, now they flee away. “Stop! Stop!” they cry, but no one turns back. [9] Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold! There is no limit to the treasure – a wealth of all precious objects. [10] She is empty, even emptiness and waste! And the heart has melted, and the knees have knocked together, and much pain is in all loins, and all their faces have become flushed. [11] Where is the den of the lions, and the feeding place of the young lions, where the lion, the lioness and the lion’s cub walked, with no one to disturb them? [12] The lion tore in pieces enough for his cubs, and strangled for his lionesses, and filled his caves with prey, and his dens with torn prey. [13] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am against you,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“and <dn>I</dn> shall burn your chariots in smoke, and the sword devour your young lions. And <dn>I</dn> shall cut off your prey from the earth, and no longer is the voice of your messengers heard.”</dq>

readings.title: Woe to the Whore
readings.subtitle: Nineveh is condemned for its violence, deceit, and sorceries.
readings.text: [Nahum 3:1] Woe to the city of blood! All of it is a lie, filled with plunder, the prey is not lacking. [2] The sound of a whip and the sound of rattling wheels, of galloping horses, of jolting chariots, [3] mounted horsemen with bright sword and glittering spear, and many wounded, and a mass of dead bodies, and no end of corpses, they stumble over the corpses – [4] because of the many whorings of the well-favoured whore, the mistress of sorceries, who sells nations by her whorings, and clans by her sorceries. [5] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am against you,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“and shall lift up your skirts over your face, and shall show nations your nakedness, and reigns your shame.</dq> [6] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall cast abominations upon you, and treat you as foolish, and make a spectacle of you.</dq> [7] <dq>“And it shall be that all who see you flee from you, and say, ‘Ninevěh is laid waste! Who does mourn for her?’ Where do <dn>I</dn> seek comforters for you?”</dq>

readings.title: A Warning from Thebes
readings.subtitle: Nineveh's fate will be like that of the great Egyptian city, which also fell despite its strength.
readings.text: [8] Are you better than No Amon, who dwelt by the Nile-streams, with waters around her, whose rampart was like the sea, whose wall was like the sea? [9] Kush and Mitsrayim were her strength, even unlimited. Put and Luḇim were your helpers. [10] Yet she was exiled, she went into captivity. At the head of every street her young children were dashed to pieces. Lots were cast for her esteemed men, and all her great men were bound in chains. [11] You too are to become drunk, you are to go into hiding. You too are to seek refuge from the enemy. [12] All your strongholds are fig trees with ripened figs, when shaken they shall fall into the mouth of the eater. [13] See, your people in your midst are women! The gates of your land shall be opened wide to your enemies. Fire shall consume your gate bars.

readings.title: Your Injury Has No Healing
readings.subtitle: Nineveh's leaders are asleep, its people are scattered, and its wound is grievous.
readings.text: [14] Draw for yourself water for the siege! Strengthen your defences! Go into the clay and tread the mortar, lay hold of the brick mould! [15] There a fire shall consume you, a sword cut you off, eat you up like a locust. Make yourself many like the locust, make yourself many like the swarming locust! [16] You have increased your merchants more than the stars of the heavens. The locust shall strip off and fly away. [17] Your officials are like the locusts, and your marshals are like the great grasshoppers, which settle in the hedges on a cold day – when the sun rises they flee away, and the place where they are is unknown. [18] Your shepherds have slumbered, O sovereign of Ashshur, your nobles lie down to rest. Your people are scattered on the mountains, and no one gathers them. [19] Your injury has no healing, your wound is grievous. All who hear news of you shall clap their hands over you. For over whom did your evil not pass continually?
